user_prompt:
In square EFGH, which of these is FALSE?

[Image: Square EFGH with diagonals]

Figure, described in words:
A square EFGH with vertices labeled: bottom-left vertex E, bottom-right vertex F, top-right vertex G, and top-left vertex H. Both diagonals, EG and HF, are drawn, intersecting at an interior point labeled I.

A. ΔEIF and ΔEIH are congruent.
B. ΔGHI and ΔGHF are congruent.
C. ΔEFH and ΔEGH are congruent.
D. ΔEIF and ΔGIH are congruent.

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
answer.title: Answer

llm_thinking:
I'm working through the square EFGH diagonal properties, checking triangle congruences by comparing sides formed by the intersection point I, starting with EIF and EIH being congruent by SSS, then examining whether GHI and GHF share the same relationship.

Since I lies strictly inside diagonal HF, triangle GHI only covers half the area of GHF—they can't be congruent, so option B is false. Checking the remaining options: EFH and EGH match up via their right angles and shared leg EH (true), and EIF/GIH satisfy SAS through vertical angles at I (true), confirming B is the sole false statement.
